TERRAIN — Road Network Intelligence Product

End-to-end satellite imagery → road network → resilience analytics. Prepared for prospective licensing client · Team Nebula Decoders · ISRO Bharatiya Antariksh Hackathon 2026 (PS4)

Executive summary

TERRAIN ingests raw satellite tiles, automatically extracts the road network with a fine-tuned Swin-UNet segmentation model, converts it into a topologically-connected graph, heals discontinuities caused by clouds, shadows, canopy and bare ground, and ranks the network's most critical, failure-sensitive junctions (gatekeepers). Emitted resilience index — a 0–1 score — lets an operator quantify how robust a city's road network is to the loss of its most important nodes. This report demonstrates the pipeline on three operational sensors across three Indian cities.

What the pipeline delivers

Satellite tile → Segmentation → Skeletonization → Graph build → Topological healing → Gatekeeper analysis → Resilience index
100%largest connected component after healing (worst 96%)
≤200 mhard cap enforced on every healed gap
0.58–0.79resilience index achieved across cities
3satellite sensors · 3 cities demonstrated

The healing pass fuses an initially fragmented network (hundreds of disconnected road fragments) into a single coherent component by inserting occlusion bridges, with angular smoothness gates and a hard 200 m physics-validated gap cap. Gatekeepers are the junctions whose removal most degrades global connectivity.

City-by-city visual

Cartosat-3 · Hyderabad (1 m GSD, optical)

Resolution: very high-resolution optical · 1 m ground sampling — reveals fine street geometry, lane detail and cul-de-sacs under heavy canopy/shadow occlusion.

Sentinel-2 · Bengaluru (10 m GSD, multispectral)

Resolution: 10 m multispectral · wide revisit coverage of the road arterial skeleton at neighbourhood scale; occlusion from clouds and mixed urban texture is the dominant failure to heal.

LISS-IV · Delhi (5.8 m GSD, multispectral)

Resolution: 5.8 m multispectral (ISRO RESOURCESAT-2) · balanced mid-resolution view of the inter-urban grid; fragmentation from secondary roads and dense built-up shading is recovered by healing.

Why the numbers matter for a buyer

Complete networks, not fragments. Competitive solutions leave satellite road maps broken by occlusion; TERRAIN's healing closes valid gaps under a strict distance limit and planarizes crossings, yielding usable topology for routing and GIS.
Operational resilience scoring. The resilience index and gatekeeper ranking turn a raw map into actionable prioritisation for transport planning, emergency routing and infrastructure investment.
Sensor-agnostic. Demonstrated on 1 m very-high-res, 5.8 m and 10 m satellites — the same model stack adapts to any release cadence or archive.

Model & engineering appendix

  • Segmentation: Swin-UNet (timm swin_tiny encoder, 4-band stem) fine-tuned with composite Focal+Dice+Boundary+Connectivity loss, adaptive per-tile anti-flood threshold to suppress false "road everywhere" predictions.
  • Graph: medial-axis skeletonization → deterministic node/edge chain graph (NetworkX).
  • Healing: multi-pass KD-tree nearest-endpoint + DSUcycle-guard + angular gates (90°/relaxed), planarization at crossings, isolated-pixel recovery.
  • Criticality: betweenness centrality (train-time pseudo-labels) + inductive 2-layer GCN for live gatekeeper ranking; node-removal cascade → resilience index in [0, 1].
